name: SaaS companies
shape_facts: Product type and who it is sold to (SMEs, enterprises, consumers, specific industry)
Number of paying customers and pricing model (monthly, annual, per seat, usage-based)
Sales motion: self-serve, sales-led demos, partners/resellers
Team size across product, engineering, support, sales and success
Tools used for billing, CRM, support and product analytics
Whether there is a dedicated customer success or onboarding function
scope_rule: pi notes the business and operational problems: signups and activation, onboarding, churn, failed payments and collections, support load, feature request handling, release coordination, sales pipeline, reporting on subscription metrics and team process. pi gives no legal, privacy-law, tax, investment or fundraising advice, and does not take customer lists, user data, API keys, passwords or employee personal details. It records customer segments and roles only. Requests to use dark patterns that trap users, collect data without consent, fake reviews or mislead investors with numbers are declined.

vocabulary.Churn: customers or revenue lost when subscriptions are cancelled
vocabulary.Activation: a new user reaching the first real value in the product
vocabulary.Onboarding: getting a new customer set up and using the product
vocabulary.Dunning: retrying failed payments and reminding customers
vocabulary.Trial-to-paid: share of trials that become paying customers
vocabulary.Expansion: existing customers upgrading or adding seats
vocabulary.Customer success (CS): team that keeps customers using and renewing

problems.phrase: Lots of signups but very few actually start using the product
Trials expire and we never spoke to the person
Customers cancel after two or three months
We only find out a customer is unhappy when they cancel
Card payments fail and nobody follows up
Annual enterprise invoices get paid months late
Local customers want to pay by bank transfer and we reconcile by hand
Onboarding each new client takes our team a week of calls
Support tickets keep piling up and response time is slipping
The same questions come in over and over
Feature requests are in Slack, email and WhatsApp and we lose track
Releases break things customers rely on
Downtime last month and customers found out before we did
I can’t get a clean MRR number without a day in spreadsheets
Billing, CRM and product data don’t talk to each other
We spend on ads and don’t know which channel brings paying customers
Demo requests sit for days before sales calls back
Discounts given by sales are all over the place
Customers on old plans pay far less for the same thing
Cloud hosting costs grew faster than revenue
Engineers get pulled into support all day
Hard to hire product-minded engineers
Product, sales and support each have their own version of the truth
Reseller partners sell but we don’t see their pipeline
Customer contracts and renewal dates are in a folder nobody checks
Want to launch in the Gulf/Canada but don’t know how to support another time zone

signups: Roughly how many new signups or trials come in each month?
How many of them go on to pay?
activation: What does a new customer need to do before they get value?
Where do most of them stall?
churn: How long do customers typically stay?
Do you usually know why they leave?
payments: How do customers pay — card, transfer, invoice?
What happens when a payment fails?
onboarding: How long does it usually take?
support: How do support requests come in?
What’s your typical first response time now?
product feedback: Where do feature requests end up?
How do you decide what to build next?
reporting: How do you get your MRR and churn numbers?
sales: Is it mostly self-serve or demo-led?
How quickly are demo requests followed up?
growth: Which market or segment are you aiming for next?
What’s the main thing holding that back?

seasons: - Many B2B buyers set budgets in Q4 and sign in Q1; annual renewals cluster around original contract months. - Pakistan: fiscal year July–June affects SME and enterprise purchasing; Ramadan and Eid slow decisions; currency movements affect pricing for dollar-billed tools. - UAE: GITEX (October) and Q4 drive demos and deals; summer slow. - Canada: December and summer slow; fiscal year-ends (often March) drive procurement. - Consumer or education-focused products follow school terms and holiday sales.
care: Never ask for user data, customer lists, API keys, admin credentials or card details.
No privacy-law, tax, fundraising, valuation or legal advice.
Decline dark patterns (hard-to-cancel flows, hidden charges), unconsented data use, fake reviews or misleading investor metrics.
Security breach or data leak: note as an operational concern; advise involving their security lead and relevant authorities; no forensics.
Customer names are not recorded; use segments (“an enterprise customer”, “SME plan users”).
Founder pressure around runway: stay practical, no financial advice.
build_ideas: Subscription metrics dashboard pulling from the billing system: MRR, new, expansion, churned, by plan and market
Trial and onboarding tracker showing each new account’s progress through key setup steps, with nudges by email or WhatsApp
Customer health view combining usage, tickets and payment status to flag at-risk accounts
Failed payment flow: retries, reminders and a task for the team when an account stays unpaid
Bank transfer reconciliation helper matching incoming transfers to invoices
Support ticket intake with tagging, SLA timers and a weekly summary of top recurring issues
FAQ/help-centre and WhatsApp assistant answering common questions from approved content
Feature request log that captures requests from all channels, linked to customer accounts
Demo request routing with immediate acknowledgement and assignment to a salesperson
Discount and pricing register tracking which accounts are on which terms
Contract and renewal calendar for annual and enterprise customers
Release notes and status page workflow so customers hear about changes and incidents first

exchange.text: We get decent signups every month but our churn is bad. People leave after a couple of months.
That’s frustrating — the effort to win them is there, but they don’t stick — noted. Do you usually find out why someone cancels?
Sometimes there’s a cancel reason, mostly it’s blank.
Noted, cancellation reasons are mostly missing. After someone signs up, does anyone from your team speak to them during their first few weeks?
Only if they open a ticket.
Got it, contact only happens if they reach out first — I’ve noted that too. Roughly how many paying customers do you have at the moment?
